quadratic.title: What is a Quadratic Equation?
quadratic.intro: A quadratic equation is an equation where the highest power of the variable is 2 (squared).
quadratic.discovery: Imagine throwing a basketball—its path through the air forms a curve called a parabola. Quadratic equations describe this beautiful curved motion!
quadratic.standardForm: Standard form of a quadratic equation:
quadratic.where: where a ≠ 0 (a, b, c are constants)

parabola.title: Understanding Parabolas
parabola.intro: The graph of a quadratic function is a U-shaped curve called a parabola. Let's explore its key features!

factoring.title: Solving by Factoring
factoring.intro: When a quadratic can be factored, it's often the quickest solution method. The idea: if (x + a)(x + b) = 0, then either factor must equal zero!

formula.title: The Quadratic Formula
formula.intro: The quadratic formula is the ultimate weapon—it works for ANY quadratic equation!
formula.works: This formula always works, even when factoring is difficult or impossible.

completing.title: Completing the Square
completing.intro: This method converts any quadratic into a perfect square form. It's like solving a puzzle to reveal the solutions!

example3.title: Example 3: Real-World Projectile
example3.problem: A ball is thrown upward with height h(t) = -16t² + 64t feet after t seconds. When does it hit the ground?
example3.answer: The ball hits the ground at t = 4 seconds (t = 0 is when it was thrown)

mistake1.title: Forgetting the ± in the Quadratic Formula
mistake1.wrong: Students write only the + part of ±:
mistake1.correct: The ± symbol means TWO solutions (one with +, one with -):
mistake1.explanation: The ± symbol is there because quadratics can have up to 2 solutions! You must calculate both the addition and subtraction to find all solutions.
mistake1.tip: Think of ± as "plus OR minus"—it gives you two separate calculations to do!

mistake2.title: Sign Errors When Factoring
mistake2.correct: Check: what two numbers multiply to +6 and add to -5? Answer: -2 and -3
mistake2.explanation: When factoring, you need two numbers that multiply to give c AND add to give b. Both conditions must be satisfied! Check your factors by expanding.

mistake3.title: Confusing Vertex with Y-Intercept
mistake3.wrong: Students think the vertex is always at x = 0:
mistake3.correct: The vertex x-coordinate is found using the formula:
mistake3.explanation: The y-intercept is where x = 0, but the vertex is the turning point, found at x = -b/(2a). These are usually different points!

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
realWorld.intro: Quadratics model countless real-world phenomena—from sports to business to physics!

app1.title: 🏀 Projectile Motion
app1.description: Any object thrown through the air follows a parabolic path.
app1.example: Basketball shot, water fountain arc, rocket trajectory all use quadratics: h(t) = -16t² + v₀t + h₀

app2.title: 💰 Business Profit Maximization
app2.description: Companies use quadratics to find maximum profit.
app2.example: If profit P = -2x² + 100x - 500, the vertex formula finds the optimal production level

app3.title: 🏛️ Architecture & Design
app3.description: Parabolic arches are used in bridges and buildings for strength.
app3.example: The Gateway Arch in St. Louis, suspension bridges, and satellite dishes all use parabolic curves

challenge.title: Challenge Problem
challenge.description: Apply quadratics to a real-world scenario!

exercise1.question: Solve by factoring: x² + 5x + 6 = 0. What are the solutions?

exercise2.question: What is the discriminant (b² - 4ac) for x² - 6x + 9 = 0? Enter the value.
exercise2.explanation: b² - 4ac = 36 - 36 = 0. Discriminant of 0 means one repeated solution

exercise3.question: Solve using the quadratic formula: x² - x - 6 = 0
exercise3.explanation: Using formula: x = (1 ± √25)/2 = (1 ± 5)/2, so x = 3 or x = -2

exercise4.question: For f(x) = x² - 4x + 3, what is the x-coordinate of the vertex?

exercise5.question: How many real solutions does x² + 2x + 5 = 0 have?

exercise6.question: A garden has length 3m more than width. Area is 28 m². What is the width? Enter the value.
exercise6.hint: Let w = width. Length = w + 3. Area: w(w + 3) = 28
exercise6.explanation: w² + 3w - 28 = 0. Factor: (w + 7)(w - 4) = 0. Width must be positive, so w = 4 meters

notes.title: Tips & Strategies
notes.tip1: 📝 Try factoring first—it's fastest when it works! If factoring seems difficult, use the quadratic formula.
notes.tip2: 🎯 The discriminant tells you: positive = 2 solutions, zero = 1 solution, negative = 0 real solutions.
notes.tip3: 💡 Always check your solutions by substituting back into the original equation!

conclusion.title: You've Conquered Quadratics! 🎉
conclusion.summary: Quadratic equations are fundamental to physics, engineering, business, and advanced mathematics. You now have three powerful methods: factoring, the quadratic formula, and completing the square. These skills will serve you throughout your STEM journey!
conclusion.takeaway1: Quadratic equations: ax² + bx + c = 0 where a ≠ 0
conclusion.takeaway2: Three methods: factoring, quadratic formula, completing the square
conclusion.takeaway3: Discriminant determines number of real solutions
conclusion.takeaway4: Quadratics model parabolic motion, optimization, and real-world phenomena
